_note: DRAFT handoff questions and answer keys, written from the case files on 2026-11-26. Review each one in your own clinical words before any session. Q1-Q3 are scored automatically (exact, or within the tolerance); Q4 is scored 0-2 afterwards with the rubric. Rising/Falling/Stable trend questions compare the latest value with the value 12 h before handoff. All three of those keys are Falling, so before the study the clinical reviewers should change one to a Rising or Stable key; otherwise a participant who always answers Falling scores 3 of 3.

questions.text: What is the most recent potassium?
Compared with 12 hours before handoff, is the heart rate now rising, falling or stable?
questions.source: Range 71-98 bpm over 12 h; latest 81 bpm, down 16 from 12 h earlier

questions.text: At what time is the next oxycodone dose given after handoff?
questions.source: eMAR: oxycodone 5 mg given 21:37 (next 12 h used as a stand-in for due)

questions.text: What is your top safety concern for the next 12 hours, and what data support it?

rubric.2: Names bleeding risk on the heparin infusion after a vascular procedure complication, with at least one supporting value (Hgb 9.3, platelets 146, the procedure-related diagnosis codes), or names hypokalemia (K 3.2) with its value and the need to replace and recheck.
rubric.1: Names a relevant concern (bleeding, anticoagulation, low potassium, pain control) without supporting data.
rubric.0: No concern, or one not supported by this patient's data.
